title: whisper.swiftui example not working
body:
When I run the whisper.swiftui example compiled in Xcode, transcription fails with:

About to run whisper_full
whisper_full_with_state: failed to encode
Failed to run the model

I am using ggml-base.en.bin. The whisper.objc sample works on the same machine with the same model. This is on a 16 GB M1 MacBook Pro.

symptoms_visible: The SwiftUI example reaches whisper_full and then prints 'whisper_full_with_state: failed to encode' and 'Failed to run the model'.
The Objective-C sample works on the same M1 MacBook Pro with the same ggml-base.en.bin model.
N0.label: N0 SwiftUI encoding failure reported

symptoms_visible: After changing the Metal library lookup to use the existing default.metallib, I can see the Metal device initialize and its buffers allocate, but transcription still prints the same failed-to-encode error.
N1_x.label: N1_x Metal-loading change aftermath

symptoms_visible: Metal loads and allocates buffers from the GGML dependency, but the SwiftUI transcription still fails during encoding.
N2.label: N2 correct package edit confirmed

symptoms_visible: My last test of the existing Swift package versions still fails at whisper_full even though Metal initializes.
N3.label: N3 GGML API synchronization available

symptoms_visible: After updating the Swift packages to their latest versions, the SwiftUI example transcribes successfully and no longer reports the failed-to-encode error.
N_terminal.label: N_terminal reporter confirmed transcription fixed

symptoms_visible: After updating the Swift packages to their latest versions, the SwiftUI example transcribes successfully and no longer reports the failed-to-encode error.
N_terminal_direct.label: N_terminal_direct fixed without Metal detour

solution.intent: Treat the transcription failure as a missing Metal-library resource and change GGML to load the default.metallib produced by Xcode.
solution.concrete_example: Change GGML's Metal loader to look for default.metallib, then rebuild the SwiftUI application and retry transcription.

edges.comment: Reporter jeybee c4 and c7: the reporter manually changed the GGML Metal lookup, observed successful Metal initialization and buffer allocation, but the original encoding failure remained. This falsifies Metal resource loading as the cause of the reported transcription failure, although the thread later treats Metal packaging as a separate issue.

question_patterns: Did you make that source change in whisper.cpp itself or in the GGML package used by the Swift package?
Which package's Metal loader did you edit?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I changed it in GGML, which is what the Swift package uses. The log shows that it loads Metal and allocates the Metal buffers, but transcription still fails.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I only changed the copy in whisper.cpp; the Swift package is still using an unchanged GGML dependency and still cannot initialize Metal.
I changed the GGML dependency and Metal initializes, but my log has slightly different buffer sizes.

edges.comment: Maintainer ggerganov c5 asked which copy was changed; reporter jeybee c7 confirmed the edit was in the GGML dependency and supplied the raw observation that Metal loaded while encoding still failed.

solution.intent: Synchronize the GGML dependency with whisper.cpp because their APIs had diverged, causing the Swift package's encoding call to fail independently of Metal-library loading.
solution.concrete_example: Bring the GGML package implementation back into sync with the API expected by whisper.cpp, then publish that synchronized package for the SwiftUI example.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter established only that the correct GGML package could initialize Metal while whisper_full still failed. The maintainer found the API divergence by comparing the whisper.cpp and GGML sources; that diagnosis is engineer inference, not something the reporter measured.

edges.comment: Maintainer ggerganov c8: source investigation found that whisper.cpp and the standalone GGML package had diverged. The maintainer synchronized GGML and reported that the SwiftUI example then worked. The unresolved metallib packaging concern was explicitly separate because failure to load it merely caused CPU fallback.

solution.intent: Update the Xcode Swift package dependencies to receive the synchronized GGML API, rerun the SwiftUI example, and require the reporter to confirm transcription before declaring resolution.
solution.concrete_example: In Xcode, use File -> Packages -> Update to Latest Package Versions, rebuild the SwiftUI example, and report whether the same audio now transcribes without the failed-to-encode message.

edges.comment: Maintainer instruction in c8 and reporter confirmation in c12: jeybee updated the Swift packages after the GGML synchronization and explicitly confirmed that this fixed the reported issue.

solution.intent: Recognize the known API mismatch between whisper.cpp and its GGML Swift-package dependency, synchronize the dependency, then have the reporter update Xcode packages and verify transcription.
solution.concrete_example: Use the synchronized GGML package, choose File -> Packages -> Update to Latest Package Versions in Xcode, rebuild, and confirm that whisper_full can transcribe successfully.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut represents proposing the thread's accepted fix immediately. The API divergence is the maintainer's source-level diagnosis; the skipped Metal experiment is useful disambiguating evidence but is not required when the known package mismatch is recognized.

edges.comment: Shortcut copy of the accepted resolution for an agent that diagnoses the package API mismatch from the opening report without first following the thread's falsified Metal-resource direction. Reporter verification from c12 is still required.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: the whisper.cpp Swift package and its GGML dependency had diverged at the API level, causing whisper_full encoding to fail.
The fix must synchronize the GGML dependency and have the user update the Swift packages in Xcode before rebuilding the SwiftUI example.

Must not present changing the lookup from ggml.metallib to default.metallib as the fix for the reported transcription failure; the reporter successfully initialized Metal that way and still saw the same encoding error.
Must distinguish the separate Metal-resource packaging issue from the encoding failure: inability to load the metallib could cause CPU fallback, but it was not the accepted cause of this report.
Must ask the reporter to retest after updating the packages and must not declare the issue resolved until the reporter confirms that transcription works.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Apple-platform developer who can build SwiftUI and Objective-C examples in Xcode, edit dependency source, and interpret Metal initialization logs.
persona_hint.communication_style: Concise and evidence-driven; reports exact log behavior, answers package-location questions directly, and confirms the successful fix promptly.
